correctness.rationale: Correctness PASS: independent re-execution confirms the finite census. itertools brute force to n=8 gives 1,1,2,6,22,90,394,1806,8558; n=9 gives 41586 vs 41586 with balanced differences 16074 vs 16074; recompiled census.c reproduces counts to n=12 (206098,1037718,5293446) and naive.c agrees to n=9; all 14 archived witnesses n=8..14 verified by independent O(n^4) pattern test to lie in exactly one class with both-avoiding parent; dihedral exclusion re-verified (no map sends {1342,1423} to {1342,1432}). The DRAFT honestly labels growth-rate equality and Wilf-equivalence as conjectures, distinguishing evidence from proof. Residual single-engine dependence for n=13..14 is mitigated by exact Schröder/OEIS match.

originality.rationale: Originality FAIL. EMERGENT_FINDING genuinely arose from target work on the same pair (deeper census after blocked separation), not a convenient replacement, so route is legitimate — but the headline is not new. ADMISSION_DEFECT: Admission claimed no database/theorem covers Av(1342,1423) vs Av(1342,1432), yet Kremer (2000) via Homberger Ch.9 proves Av(1342,1423) is counted by the large Schröder numbers with gf (1-x-sqrt(1-6x+x^2))/2, and the public TileScope/PermPAL record (June 2019) explicitly lists BOTH Av(1342,1432) and Av(1342,1423) among 2x4 classes enumerated by the Schröder numbers, with PermPAL claiming all 56 two-pattern length-4 classes have specifications. Same Schröder gf implies identical counts for ALL n, so coincidence to n=14, balanced differences (|A\B|=|B\A| follows automatically from equal finite totals), and routine witnesses are a recomputation/certificate of a known stronger infinite enumeration, not a new boundary. A timestamp or failed OEIS literal-title search does not establish priority.

value.rationale: Value FAIL under the shared STANDARD with no preset presumption for EMERGENT_FINDING. The object pair was motivated, but the invariant (exact counts to n=14: 1,1,2,6,22,90,394,1806,8558,41586,206098,1037718,5293446,27297738,142078746) is already known and mechanically implied: termwise it equals the large Schröder sequence OEIS A006318 (verified: submitted[n]=A006318[n-1] for n>=1, b-file to n=2000 contains 142078746 and beyond). This is known-database recomputation / arbitrary finite slice of a known infinite enumeration, explicitly rejected by the STANDARD. Certification (dual engines, witnesses, symmetry check) strengthens evidence but does not create value by itself, and no new general theorem, boundary, redirect, or downstream use survives once Schröder coverage is recognized — the redirect was already available from Kremer/TileScope.

broader_coverage.evidence: Kremer 2000 abstract via Semanticscholar: 'exactly 10 classes enumerated by the large Schroder numbers'; Homberger cites Kremer for Av(1342,1423)-Schroder; TileScope June 2019 explicitly places both Av(1342,1432) and Av(1342,1423) in the Schroder 2x4 list; PermPAL/Combinatorial Exploration (arXiv:2202.07715) claims all 56 two-pattern length-4 classes specified. Together these constitute a broader classification covering the submitted pair as a special case.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader theorem/database exhaustively covering the pair as Schröder members logically entails identical enumeration for every n, hence the finite n<=14 coincidence is a strict special case/corollary of that coverage, not an independent discovery.

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Prior Av(1342,1423) Schroder gf f(x)=(1-x-sqrt(1-6x+x^2))/2 (Kremer via Homberger) plus prior Av(1342,1432) Schroder enumeration (TileScope/PermPAL) share one generating function, therefore identical coefficients for all n; equal finite totals automatically force balanced one-sided differences and make explicit witnesses routine brute-force certificates.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The submitted headline (identical counts, balanced differences, witnesses) is mechanically implied by the conjunction of the two prior Schroder enumerations; it is a recomputation/certificate/repackaging of that known stronger infinite fact, so prior implication defeats novelty even though no prior states the n=14 table verbatim.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: whether known Av(1342,1423) and Av(1342,1432) Schroder enumerations imply identical counts and balanced differences to n=14

equivalent_formulations.evidence: Homberger/Kremer give the analytic form f(x)=(1-x-sqrt(1-6x+x^2))/2 for Av(1342,1423); TileScope gives the same Schroder enumeration for Av(1342,1432); hence transfer-matrix spectral radii, dominant singularities (3-2*sqrt(2)), and insertion-language entropies coincide. No separate spectral/singularity ordering exists to discover.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Checking dual spectral, singularity, and entropic phrasings closes the renaming loophole: all equivalent formulations collapse to one shared Schroder singularity, so the claim cannot be novel under synonymous notation or encoding.
equivalent_formulations.search: Av(1342,1423) versus Av(1342,1432) spectral radius singularity generating-function entropy Schroder equivalence

exact_database_or_table.evidence: OEIS A006318 b-file (n=0..2000, Fung Lam) contains 206098,1037718,5293446,27297738,142078746 at shifted indices; audit verified submitted n=0..14 equals A006318[n-1] termwise; OEIS text search for the submitted tails returns only A006318. No separate Av(1342,1423)/Av(1342,1432) table is needed because both are rows of the Schroder table.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The exact parameters appear in an official database table, so the census is known-database recomputation rather than a new table; extending the admitted n<=9 anchor to n=14 adds only further known Schroder terms already stored to n=2000.
